label: POOL Qwen3-14B, --max-num-batched-tokens sweep (the 14B check bin/lab asks for before trusting 512)
status: MEASURED 2026-10-02 00:13-00:26 (4 restarts, all exit 0); predictions above were committed (4fe2c8b) before the first restart
why: bin/lab defaults POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS to 512 from the 70B sweep (bench/baseline-pool-llama31-70b-prefill-batch.json: TTFT at 3,950 tokens 4.74 / 5.16 / 6.08 / 7.81 s and KV 4.38x / 4.12x / 3.86x / 3.09x for 512 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096). Its comment says: 'Untested on the 14B: with 5x fewer parameters per chunk, the fixed cost of each step (the hop across the link, scheduling, eager kernel launches) is a bigger share, so its best width may be larger. Run bench/prefill_curve.py before trusting 512 there.' Qwen3-14B is bin/lab's default pool model.

method.design: Four full pool restarts with bin/lab's defaults (Qwen/Qwen3-14B, max-model-len 8192, gpu-memory-utilization 0.92) except POOL_MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS = 4096, 1024, 2048, 512, in that order. bench/prefill_sweep.sh runs each: lab pool up, the head's KV lines from /tmp/vllm-pool.log, one throwaway request, bench/prefill_curve.py (default counts, 3 samples, unique random prompts so the prefix cache cannot serve one), lab pool down.
method.not_measured: Decode throughput (the 70B showed it indifferent to B at c=5, 16 and 128); long prompts under concurrency.

preregistered_predictions.kv: INFERENCE: KV falls monotonically as B rises, as on the 70B (the prefill activation buffers come out of the same budget); 512 has the most.
preregistered_predictions.ttft_at_3950: INFERENCE: 4096 is the slowest (one chunk for the whole prompt, no pipeline overlap). The curve is flatter than the 70B's, whose 512 -> 4096 spread is +65%; 512 is the fastest or within 10% of the fastest.
preregistered_predictions.decision_rule: 512 stays the 14B default unless another B is faster at the longest prompt by more than the larger of the two 3-sample ranges AND keeps at least 95% of 512's KV tokens. A different winner is a proposal for bin/lab (per-model default), not a change made here.

verdict: 512 stays the 14B default. It is the fastest width at every prompt length from 983 tokens up (at 3,923 tokens: 1.032 s vs 1.166 / 1.348 / 1.666 s for 1024 / 2048 / 4096; 3-sample ranges <= 0.003 s) and has the most KV. bin/lab's guess that the 14B's best width 'may be larger' is refuted. Unlike the 70B, the KV cost of a wider batch is small here (1.5% from 512 to 4096, vs 29%).

kv_cost_of_the_prefill_batch.note: From the head's /tmp/vllm-pool.log ('Available KV cache memory' per stage; 'GPU KV cache size' is the engine's budget, set by the smaller stage).

outcome_vs_predictions.kv: CONFIRMED monotone (60,832 -> 59,936 tokens), but small: 1.5% across the sweep, not the 70B's 29%.
outcome_vs_predictions.ttft_at_3950: PARTLY WRONG. 4096 slowest and 512 fastest: confirmed. 'Flatter than the 70B's': wrong, +61.5% vs +65%; the 14B's curve has the 70B's shape.
outcome_vs_predictions.decision_rule: No width beats 512, so 512 stays; nothing to propose for bin/lab beyond updating its 'untested on the 14B' comment.

provenance.measured_from: laptop (lab-laptop), bench/prefill_sweep.sh with the deployed bin/lab at fb87b44
provenance.final_state: pool down after each width. 'lab pool down' does NOT restart llama-swap (it prints 'lab up' for that); before the sweep the desktop's llama-swap was active and the laptop's inactive, so the desktop's needs 'lab up' afterwards (done after G7b, which used the desktop card next).
